info.desc: Metal Box is the second studio album by Public Image Ltd, released by Virgin Records on 23 November 1979. The album takes its name from the round metal canister which contained the initial pressings of the record. It was later reissued in standard vinyl packaging as Second Edition in February 1980 by Virgin Records in the United Kingdom, and by Warner Bros. Records and Island Records in the United States. The album was a departure from PiL's 1978 debut First Issue, with the band moving into a more avant-garde sound characterised by John Lydon's cryptic lyrics, propulsive dub-inspired rhythms led .

podcast.body: *Metal Box* is considered a masterpiece and one of the biggest ruptures in music history. It featured incredible bass lines from Jah Wobble, acting as both rhythmic pulse and melodic motif, creating physical and heavy lows described as "the human heartbeat." Keith Levene, freed from traditional rhythm and melody duties, played dislocatedly, producing crystalline and kaleidoscopic sounds. "Y ahora sí, hablemos de esta obra maestra, Metalbox."

podcast.body: For *Metal Box*, Public Image Ltd fully embraced the methodologies of disco and Jamaican dub, using the recording studio as an instrument in itself. They radically processed sounds, employed echo chambers, and incorporated immense empty spaces, treating silence as equally important as noise. "Abrazaron del todo la metodología de la música disco y del tapjamaicano, o sea que usaban el estudio de grabación como si fueran instrumentos más."

podcast.body: Released in the winter of 1979, *Metal Box* was presented not as a conventional record but as a metallic 16mm film canister, devoid of band photos. This weighty, hard-to-store, and more expensive object was intentionally "hostile to the consumer," a deliberate choice by John Lydon. "Se encontraron con esto, una caja metálica de película de 16 milímetros, sin fotos de la banda, que pesaban montón, que era incómoda de almacenar en las estanterías y para colmo era mucho más caro que un disco normal."

podcast.body: The metallic box packaging of *Metal Box* served as a symbol of a radical break from the punk scene that had dominated two years prior. Its release marked the birth of something new, rejecting punk's rules, limits, and dogmas, and forging a new path for music. "esta caja metálica no era solo una lecdota, sino que era un símbolo, el símbolo de una ruptura con una escena que había arrasado dos años antes, el punk."

podcast.body: This album was released in an unconventional literal metal box, containing six sides of 12-inch vinyl, each spinning at 45 RPM. It is considered one of the most important post-punk releases for pushing conventional musical limits, showcasing deep bass, Eno's influence, and even disco elements, alongside repetitive music influenced by Krautrock. "In 1979, Public Image Limited released an album called Metal Box."
